lessons.title: Meet the Editor
lessons.description: Your first steps in the code editor: files, folders, saving, the terminal, and running a program. No experience needed.

checkpoints.title: Make a folder
checkpoints.description: Make a new folder called my-team.

checkpoints.title: Make a file
checkpoints.description: Make a file called about.txt inside my-team, with a sentence in it.

checkpoints.title: Rename a file
checkpoints.description: Rename untitled.txt to team.txt.

checkpoints.title: Delete a file
checkpoints.description: Delete delete-me.txt.

checkpoints.title: Run a program
checkpoints.description: Put your name in Main.java and run it.

lessons.title: Git Basics
lessons.description: Commit, branch, merge, resolve a conflict, rebase, then push, pull and stash across eight small scenario repos.

checkpoints.title: First commit
checkpoints.description: Add your name to roster.txt and commit it with a real message.

checkpoints.title: Feature branch
checkpoints.description: Branch off develop as issue-12-<description> and make at least two commits.

checkpoints.title: Merge
checkpoints.description: Merge the finished issue-7-auto-distance branch into develop.

checkpoints.title: Merge conflict
checkpoints.description: Merge issue-9-max-speed into develop and resolve the conflict.

checkpoints.title: Rebase
checkpoints.description: Rebase issue-15-led-colors onto the latest develop.

checkpoints.title: Push
checkpoints.description: Push the issue-18-team-colors branch to origin.

checkpoints.title: Pull
checkpoints.description: Pull your teammate's new commit from origin into develop.

checkpoints.title: Stash
checkpoints.description: Stash unfinished work, fix a typo on develop, then pop the stash back.

lessons.title: AdvantageScope

checkpoints.title: Flywheel line graph
checkpoints.description: A Line Graph tab plots FlywheelVelocity on its left axis.

checkpoints.title: Locked axis scale

checkpoints.title: Differentiated flywheel velocity

checkpoints.title: Game piece discrete field
checkpoints.description: GamePieceLoaded is added to the Line Graph's discrete field.

checkpoints.title: 2D field pose

checkpoints.title: 3D field pose

checkpoints.title: Swerve tab

checkpoints.title: Tuned flywheel target
checkpoints.description: FlywheelTargetVelocity was written from AdvantageScope's Tuning Mode.

lessons.title: Elastic

checkpoints.title: Counter text display

checkpoints.title: Shooter angle number slider

checkpoints.title: Climber speed number bar

checkpoints.title: Battery voltage view

checkpoints.title: Gyro heading radial gauge

checkpoints.title: Intake current graph

checkpoints.title: Match time widget
checkpoints.description: A Match Time widget is bound to MatchTimeRemaining.

checkpoints.title: Game piece boolean box
checkpoints.description: A Boolean Box widget is bound to GamePieceLoaded.

checkpoints.title: Auto routine combo box chooser

checkpoints.title: Auto routine split button chooser
checkpoints.description: A Split Button Chooser widget is bound to AutoRoutine.

checkpoints.title: Auto routine live pick

checkpoints.title: Auto delay text display
checkpoints.description: A Text Display widget bound to AutoDelaySeconds has Show Submit Button on.

checkpoints.title: Auto delay live submit
checkpoints.description: AutoDelaySeconds was submitted live from Elastic's Text Display.

checkpoints.title: Brake mode toggle button
checkpoints.description: BrakeModeEnabledButton was toggled live from Elastic's Toggle Button.

checkpoints.title: Brake mode toggle switch
checkpoints.description: BrakeModeEnabledSwitch was toggled live from Elastic's Toggle Switch.

checkpoints.title: Status single color view
checkpoints.description: A Single Color View widget is bound to StatusColorHex.

checkpoints.title: LED strip multi color view
checkpoints.description: A Multi Color View widget is bound to LedStripColorsHex.

lessons.title: Choreo
lessons.description: Build two different autonomous paths with real constraints and confirm they generate correctly.

checkpoints.title: Paths have waypoints
checkpoints.description: Every path has at least four waypoints.

checkpoints.title: Two different paths
checkpoints.description: At least two paths exist, and they aren't just copies of each other.

checkpoints.title: Path has a constraint
checkpoints.description: The path has at least one enabled constraint (Max Velocity or Max Angular Velocity; Keep In Rectangle is the default field boundary and does not count).

checkpoints.title: Path generates
checkpoints.description: Choreo successfully solves the path into a trajectory.

lessons.title: Arbor
lessons.description: Build an autonomous routine as a behavior tree: a root node, steps and their settings, a Sequence, a Timeout, a tunable value, a SubTree, and the main tree the robot runs, then replay a run that failed and find out why.

checkpoints.title: Your own tree
checkpoints.description: You created a tree of your own and saved it in the trees folder.

checkpoints.title: A Sequence of steps
checkpoints.description: A Sequence with at least three steps: a SetWantedState, a Sleep and a FollowPath.

checkpoints.title: Settings filled in
checkpoints.description: SetWantedState has a state, FollowPath has a trajectory name and Sleep has a time.

checkpoints.title: A Timeout and a Fallback
checkpoints.description: A step is wrapped in a Timeout, and a Fallback gives the tree a plan B.

checkpoints.title: A tunable value
checkpoints.description: The tree has a setting of its own, and a step uses it as {name}, so it can be tuned from the dashboard.

checkpoints.title: A SubTree
checkpoints.description: One of your trees uses another tree of yours as a SubTree, and that tree has steps in it.

checkpoints.title: The main tree
checkpoints.description: Your tree file marks the auto itself (not a SubTree) as its main tree, the one the robot runs.

checkpoints.title: Read the replay
checkpoints.description: sample-logs/Answers.java says when FollowPath finished, which node failed the auto, and which node never ran.

lessons.title: Hello, World
lessons.description: Basic java hello world project

checkpoints.title: Prints Hello, World!
checkpoints.description: Running Main prints "Hello, World!" to standard out.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.description: Declare variables, define a constant, and define your first enum.

checkpoints.title: Local variables
checkpoints.description: main() declares and prints an int, double, boolean, and String local variable.

checkpoints.title: Team name constant
checkpoints.description: A public static final TEAM_NAME constant equal to "Team 4143" (team standard: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).

checkpoints.title: Alliance enum
checkpoints.description: An Alliance enum with RED and BLUE values (team standard: UpperCamelCase type name, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE values).

checkpoints.title: Match period enum
checkpoints.description: A MatchPeriod enum with AUTONOMOUS, TELEOP, and ENDGAME values (team standard: UpperCamelCase type name, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE values).

checkpoints.title: Max speed constant
checkpoints.description: A public static final MAX_SPEED constant equal to 5.0 (team standard: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).

lessons.title: Operators
lessons.description: Do arithmetic, conversions, and comparisons with Java's operators.

checkpoints.title: Add two ints
checkpoints.description: addInts(a, b) returns a + b.

checkpoints.title: Inches to meters
checkpoints.description: inchesToMeters(inches) converts using 1 inch = 0.0254 meters.

checkpoints.title: Is even
checkpoints.description: isEven(value) uses the modulo operator to detect even numbers.

checkpoints.title: Subtract two ints
checkpoints.description: subtractInts(a, b) returns a - b.

checkpoints.title: Meters to inches
checkpoints.description: metersToInches(meters) converts using 1 inch = 0.0254 meters.

checkpoints.title: Assignment operators
checkpoints.description: applyAssignments(start) chains =, +=, -=, *=, and /= in order.

lessons.title: Conditions
lessons.description: Write if/else chains and switch statements.

checkpoints.title: Battery status
checkpoints.description: batteryStatus(percent) maps a percentage to EMPTY/LOW/MEDIUM/FULL.

checkpoints.title: Drive mode name
checkpoints.description: driveModeName(mode) uses a switch statement to name a drive mode.

checkpoints.title: Can enable
checkpoints.description: canEnable(has_comms, e_stopped) combines conditions with && and !.

checkpoints.title: Is weekend
checkpoints.description: isWeekend(day) uses || to check for Saturday or Sunday.

checkpoints.title: Motor direction
checkpoints.description: motorDirection(is_reversed) uses the ternary operator.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.description: Write for loops instead of the dangerous while loop.

checkpoints.title: Sum with a loop
checkpoints.description: sumTo(n) adds up 1..n using a for loop.

checkpoints.title: Count divisible by three
checkpoints.description: countDivisibleByThree(n) counts multiples of 3 from 1..n.

checkpoints.title: FizzBuzz
checkpoints.description: fizzBuzz(n) is the classic FizzBuzz exercise, built with a for loop.

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.description: Write methods that take and return arrays.

checkpoints.title: Array max
checkpoints.description: max(values) returns the largest element.

checkpoints.title: Array average
checkpoints.description: average(values) returns the mean as a double.

checkpoints.title: Double every element
checkpoints.description: doubleAll(values) returns a new array without mutating the input.

checkpoints.title: Array contains
checkpoints.description: contains(values, target) searches the array for a value.

checkpoints.title: Sort an array
checkpoints.description: sort(values) returns a new ascending-sorted array without mutating the input.

checkpoints.title: Fibonacci sequence
checkpoints.description: fibonacci(n) builds the first n Fibonacci numbers into a new array.

lessons.title: Methods
lessons.description: Write reusable methods, build new methods on top of them instead of copy-pasting, and practice on a few programming-course classics.

checkpoints.title: Clamp
checkpoints.description: clamp(value, min, max) squeezes value into the [min, max] range.

checkpoints.title: Scale joystick
checkpoints.description: scaleJoystick(raw_input, sensitivity) scales and clamps, reusing clamp.

checkpoints.title: Is prime
checkpoints.description: isPrime(n) returns whether n is a prime number.

checkpoints.title: Factorial
checkpoints.description: factorial(n) returns n!.

checkpoints.title: Reverse a string
checkpoints.description: reverseString(s) returns a new String with s reversed.

checkpoints.title: Is palindrome
checkpoints.description: isPalindrome(s) returns whether s reads the same backwards, reusing reverseString.

lessons.title: Debugging
lessons.description: Fix a match-log program that compiles and runs but gives wrong answers, using the debugger: breakpoints, stepping in and out, the Variables pane, conditional breakpoints, the call stack and the Pause button.

checkpoints.title: Count the stops
checkpoints.description: Answers.LOOP_RUNS_BEFORE_FIX is how many times the breakpoint in averageSpeed's loop stopped, before the fix.

checkpoints.title: Fix the average
checkpoints.description: averageSpeed adds every speed, not all but the last.

checkpoints.title: Step into a method
checkpoints.description: Accuracy.percent returns real percentages instead of 0.0.

checkpoints.title: Step out again
checkpoints.description: totalDistance adds up every leg instead of staying at 0.0.

checkpoints.title: Find the missing reading
checkpoints.description: Answers.MISSING_SAMPLE_INDEX is where the -1 is in the battery log, found with a conditional breakpoint.

checkpoints.title: Skip the missing readings
checkpoints.description: lowestVolts skips readings below 0, even when the first one is missing.

checkpoints.title: Watching a comparison
checkpoints.description: countState counts matching strings, even ones built while the program runs.

checkpoints.title: Read the stack trace
checkpoints.description: Scoring stops crashing, and each level is worth the right points.

checkpoints.title: Pause a stuck program
checkpoints.description: countValid finishes, and counts the real readings.

lessons.title: Classes & Objects
lessons.description: Build a small BankAccount class: fields, a constructor, and encapsulation - objects that protect their own state instead of exposing raw data to be mutated directly.

checkpoints.title: Deposit
checkpoints.description: deposit(amount) adds to the balance (and a negative initial balance is clamped to 0).

checkpoints.title: Withdraw
checkpoints.description: withdraw(amount) subtracts and returns true on success, or leaves the balance untouched and returns false.

checkpoints.title: Transfer
checkpoints.description: transfer(recipient, amount) moves money between two accounts, reusing withdraw and deposit.

checkpoints.title: Independent objects
checkpoints.description: Two BankAccount objects keep their own, separate state.

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.description: Solve a few problems you already solved with loops, using recursion instead - methods that call themselves down to a base case.

checkpoints.title: Factorial (recursive)
checkpoints.description: factorial(n) returns n!, computed recursively.

checkpoints.title: Fibonacci (recursive)
checkpoints.description: fibonacci(n) returns the nth Fibonacci number, computed recursively.

checkpoints.title: Sum of digits
checkpoints.description: sumDigits(n) returns the sum of n's digits, computed recursively.

checkpoints.title: Reverse a string (recursive)
checkpoints.description: reverseString(s) returns s reversed, computed recursively.

lessons.title: Inheritance
lessons.description: Extend the BankAccount class from Classes & Objects with two subclasses - one that adds a new method, one that overrides an existing one.

checkpoints.title: Savings interest
checkpoints.description: SavingsAccount.applyInterest() deposits balance * interest_rate.

checkpoints.title: Checking overdraft
checkpoints.description: CheckingAccount's overridden withdraw allows going negative up to the overdraft limit.

checkpoints.title: Checking normal withdraw
checkpoints.description: A withdrawal that never touches the overdraft still behaves like a normal withdraw.

checkpoints.title: Inherited methods
checkpoints.description: deposit, getBalance, and transfer still work as inherited, with no extra code.

lessons.title: Motors and Drivetrains
lessons.description: Drive a differential drive robot in simulation with MWLib. Learn your first Java (methods, variables, operators) while writing tank drive and arcade drive.

checkpoints.title: Your drive code
checkpoints.description: Robot.java declares its own variables and uses arithmetic for arcade drive from the left stick Y and left stick X.

checkpoints.title: Drives forward
checkpoints.description: Push the left stick forward (W) until both sides hit full speed.

checkpoints.title: Drives backward
checkpoints.description: Pull the left stick back (S) until the right side hits full reverse.

checkpoints.title: Turns in place
checkpoints.description: Push the left stick left or right (A / D) so one side drives forward and the other backward.

lessons.title: Sensors and Feedback
lessons.description: Turn encoder readings into speed and distance, ignore stick drift with an if statement, then drive exactly 2 meters with bang-bang control.

checkpoints.title: Deadband and if statements
checkpoints.description: Constants.java has a DEADBAND constant, Robot.java uses it in an if statement on each stick, and autonomousPeriodic() has an if / else.

checkpoints.title: Linear speed
checkpoints.description: Drive both sides forward at full speed. Robot/LinearSpeed should read about 5.5 m/s.

checkpoints.title: Angular speed
checkpoints.description: Spin in place at full speed (hold A, the left stick pushed left). Robot/AngularSpeed should be positive.

checkpoints.title: Drive 2 meters
checkpoints.description: Run Auto and let the robot stop. Robot/Distance should read about 2 meters (it coasts a little past, to about 2.5).

lessons.title: Drive Math and Methods
lessons.description: Move the drivetrain math into reusable methods: unit conversion, speeds, arcade drive, and an average built with an array and a for loop.

checkpoints.title: radiansToMeters
checkpoints.description: DriveMath.radiansToMeters(radians, radius) converts a wheel angle in radians to meters.

checkpoints.title: linearSpeed
checkpoints.description: DriveMath.linearSpeed(left, right) is the robot's forward speed.

checkpoints.title: angularSpeed
checkpoints.description: DriveMath.angularSpeed(left, right, trackWidth) is the robot's turning speed.

checkpoints.title: arcadeToWheelSpeeds
checkpoints.description: DriveMath.arcadeToWheelSpeeds(forward, turn) returns {left, right} and never goes past 1.0.

checkpoints.title: average
checkpoints.description: DriveMath.average(values) adds up an array with a for loop and divides by its length.

checkpoints.title: Arcade forward
checkpoints.description: In Teleop, push the left stick forward. The drivetrain should drive forward through arcadeDrive.

checkpoints.title: Arcade turn
checkpoints.description: In Teleop, push the left stick to the right (D). The right side should reverse.

checkpoints.title: Smoothed speed
checkpoints.description: Drive forward at full speed in Teleop. Robot/SmoothedSpeed should read about 5 m/s.

lessons.title: Objects and Odometry
lessons.description: Write an abstract OI class, then use WPILib kinematics and a pose estimator to track where the robot is.

checkpoints.title: OI class
checkpoints.description: OI has static getForward() and getTurn() methods, and Robot.java uses them instead of XboxController.

checkpoints.title: Chassis speeds
checkpoints.description: Drive forward at full speed. Drive/LinearSpeed (from kinematics) should read about 5 m/s.

checkpoints.title: Yaw
checkpoints.description: Spin the robot counterclockwise (left). Drive/PoseYawRad should become clearly positive.

checkpoints.title: Drive to x = 3 m
checkpoints.description: Run Auto and let the robot stop. Drive/PoseX should read about 3 meters.

lessons.title: Mechanisms and Subsystems
lessons.description: Move the drivetrain into a subsystem, then build a shooter subsystem from a flywheel and a roller mechanism.

checkpoints.title: Shooter registered
checkpoints.description: RobotContainer registers the ShooterSubsystem so it runs.

checkpoints.title: Shooter buttons
checkpoints.description: OI reads the right bumper (shoot) and left bumper (index).

checkpoints.title: Shoot button logic
checkpoints.description: ShooterSubsystem runs the flywheel at SHOOT_DUTY_CYCLE while the shoot button is held, and stops it otherwise.

checkpoints.title: Drive from the subsystem
checkpoints.description: In Teleop, push the left stick forward. The drivetrain subsystem should drive the robot.

checkpoints.title: Flywheel spins up
checkpoints.description: Hold the shoot button. The flywheel should spin up to speed.

checkpoints.title: Roller runs
checkpoints.description: Hold the index button. The roller should run at INDEX_DUTY_CYCLE.

lessons.title: Control Theory
lessons.description: Hold the flywheel at speed three ways: bang-bang, feedforward and PID. Then tune the gains and compare how each handles a disturbance.

checkpoints.title: Bang-bang
checkpoints.description: bangBang() runs the flywheel at full power while it is too slow and stops it once it is fast enough.

checkpoints.title: Feedforward
checkpoints.description: feedforward() works out the power for the target speed from FLYWHEEL_KV.

checkpoints.title: PID selected and tuned
checkpoints.description: FLYWHEEL_CONTROL is PID with a feedforward (kV) and some feedback (kP).

checkpoints.title: Fast spin-up
checkpoints.description: With your final settings, hold the right bumper. The flywheel should reach its speed in under about 1.5 seconds.

checkpoints.title: No big overshoot
checkpoints.description: Start the robot fresh with your final settings. The flywheel should peak near its target speed, not far above it.

checkpoints.title: Recovers after a launch
checkpoints.description: Hold the right bumper until the flywheel is at speed, then tap A. It should get back to speed in under about 0.8 seconds.

lessons.title: State Machines
lessons.description: Give the shooter a state machine, and make RobotContainer the robot's own state machine that buttons ask for states.

checkpoints.title: Robot states
checkpoints.description: RobotContainer asks the drivetrain and shooter for the states each robot state needs, the right bumper asks the robot for SHOOT while held, and A simulates a launch.

checkpoints.title: Spins up before shooting
checkpoints.description: Hold the right bumper until the shooter reaches SHOOT. It must pass through SPIN_UP first (IDLE cannot jump to SHOOT).

checkpoints.title: Recovers after a launch
checkpoints.description: Hold the right bumper, then tap A. The shooter should fall back to SPIN_UP and return to SHOOT, so the shot count reaches 2.

lessons.title: Computer Vision
lessons.description: Teach the robot to see AprilTags: feed camera tag solutions to the pose estimator so the robot always knows where it is on the field, then aim at the goal from that estimate.

checkpoints.title: Camera tag solutions added
checkpoints.description: LocalizationSubsystem.updateLogic() gives each camera tag solution to the pose estimator with addVisionMeasurement(): the pose the camera saw, the time the picture was taken, and the standard deviations.

checkpoints.title: Estimate within 6 cm and 0.017 rad
checkpoints.description: Start fresh, enable Teleop and drive around (W/A/S/D) for at least 5 meters in total, with at least a quarter turn in it, then stop and wait 2 seconds. Once the robot has sat still, your estimate must be within 6 centimeters and 0.017 rad (about 1 degree) of where the robot really is. Choose better VISION_XY_STD_METERS and VISION_HEADING_STD_RADIANS if it is not.

checkpoints.title: Aim state written
checkpoints.description: DriveStates has AIM, the switch handles it with a PIDController (continuous input) that reads the pose estimate, getAngleToGoal() and isAimed() are written, and RobotContainer asks the drivetrain for AIM in the robot's AIM state.

checkpoints.title: Aims within 0.035 rad
checkpoints.description: Start fresh, enable Teleop and hold the left bumper (E). The robot should turn to face the goal and stay within 0.035 rad (about 2 degrees) of it for half a second, within 4 seconds. Raise AIM_KP if it stops short.

checkpoints.title: No wild overshoot
checkpoints.description: On that same aim, the robot must not swing more than 0.17 rad (about 10 degrees) past the goal. Lower AIM_KP or add AIM_KD to damp it.

lessons.title: Autonomous
lessons.description: Draw two paths in Choreo, then build the autonomous routine as a behavior tree in Arbor, the way the competition robot does: follow the first path, pick up, follow the second path, aim at the goal, and shoot. Then make AIM wait until the robot is really aimed.

checkpoints.title: Two paths drawn
checkpoints.description: The Choreo project has two paths that you generated, each with at least three waypoints (a start, a point in between, and an end).

checkpoints.title: Paths named ToPickup and ToScore
checkpoints.description: The paths are named ToPickup and ToScore, and your tree's FollowPath nodes drive them by those names.

checkpoints.title: Paths go where they should
checkpoints.description: ToPickup starts on the Start point and ends on the Pickup point, and ToScore starts where ToPickup ended and ends on the ScoreSpot point (each within about 30 centimeters, the join within 15).

checkpoints.title: Autonomous tree built
checkpoints.description: PickupAndScore.xml is a Sequence: FollowPath ToPickup, then FollowPath ToScore, then SetWantedState AIM and a wait for it (a Timeout holding RetryUntilSuccessful around IsSystemState AIM), then SetWantedState SHOOT, a Sleep, and SetWantedState AUTO.

checkpoints.title: AIM waits until aimed
checkpoints.description: In RobotContainer's handleStateTransition, asking for AIM puts the robot in the step state AIMING until drive_.isAimed(), and only then in AIM.

checkpoints.title: Reaches the pickup
checkpoints.description: Run PickupAndScore in Auto. The robot, measured by its true position in the simulator, should get within 0.4 meters of the Pickup point.

checkpoints.title: Reaches the scoring spot
checkpoints.description: Run PickupAndScore in Auto. The robot, measured by its true position, should get within 0.4 meters of the ScoreSpot point.

checkpoints.title: Aims before it shoots
checkpoints.description: Every shot should start with the robot truly facing the goal, within 0.087 rad (about 5 degrees). AIM has to wait until the robot is aimed before the tree moves on to SHOOT.

checkpoints.title: Shoots
checkpoints.description: The tree should get as far as shooting at least once.

lessons.title: Interfaces & Polymorphism
lessons.description: Add up a robot's battery draw: write an interface every part promises to follow, an abstract class that shares code between mechanisms, and loops that treat motors, LEDs and intakes all the same way.

checkpoints.title: The PowerUser interface
checkpoints.description: PowerUser declares getName() and getAmps(), and Motor and LedStrip implement it.

checkpoints.title: An abstract Mechanism
checkpoints.description: Mechanism is an abstract class that implements PowerUser and holds the shared name code; Intake extends it.

checkpoints.title: Total amps
checkpoints.description: PowerBudget.totalAmps adds up getAmps() for every PowerUser in an array, whatever kind it is.

checkpoints.title: Biggest user
checkpoints.description: PowerBudget.biggestUser returns the name of the part drawing the most amps, or "none" for an empty array.

lessons.title: Collections
lessons.description: Keep score at a competition: a list of match scores, a set of every team your scouts saw, and a map from team number to total points. Learn which collection fits which job.

checkpoints.title: A list of scores
checkpoints.description: ScoreList keeps scores in an ArrayList<Integer>: addScore, count, average (0.0 when empty) and best (0 when empty).

checkpoints.title: A set of teams
checkpoints.description: TeamsSeen keeps team numbers in a HashSet<Integer>, so countTeams() counts a team once even when it is added twice.

checkpoints.title: A map of totals
checkpoints.description: TeamTotals keeps a HashMap<Integer, Integer> from team number to total points; addMatch adds to the total and totalFor returns 0 for an unknown team.

checkpoints.title: Top team
checkpoints.description: TeamTotals.topTeam() returns the team with the highest total, the lower team number on a tie, or -1 with no matches.

lessons.title: Lambdas & Functional Interfaces
lessons.description: Wire up a robot's buttons and joystick the way real robot code does: write speed filters as lambdas, build new behavior out of old, and bind buttons to actions with method references.

checkpoints.title: Speed filters
checkpoints.description: SpeedFilter is a @FunctionalInterface with double apply(double speed), and Filters.half(), invert() and deadband(threshold) return lambdas.

checkpoints.title: Chain two filters
checkpoints.description: Filters.chain(first, second) returns a lambda that runs first, then runs second on the result.

checkpoints.title: Button bindings
checkpoints.description: ButtonBoard.onTrue remembers a condition and an action, and poll() runs the action once each time its condition goes from false to true.

checkpoints.title: Wire up the robot
checkpoints.description: RobotBindings binds A, B and X with method references and a lambda, and driveSpeed() is a DoubleSupplier that reads the stick every time.

lessons.title: Unit Testing
lessons.description: Write tests that prove robot math works: check a deadband, a clamp and a unit conversion with @Test and assertEquals, then catch a real shooter bug with a test before you fix it.

checkpoints.title: Test deadband
checkpoints.description: Your DriveMathTest tests pass on the real deadband and catch every buggy version the checker plants.

checkpoints.title: Test clamp
checkpoints.description: Your tests catch a clamp that forgets either end of the range, or mixes up min and max.

checkpoints.title: Test inchesToMeters
checkpoints.description: Your tests catch a wrong conversion factor, a dropped fraction and a lost minus sign.

checkpoints.title: Find the bug
checkpoints.description: ShooterMathTest has a test that fails on the buggy isAtSpeed, and ShooterMath is fixed so every test passes.

lessons.title: Exceptions
lessons.description: Read messy scouting text without crashing: throw an exception when the numbers can't be right, write your own checked exception, skip and count the bad lines, and make sure the robot always stops when an auto step fails.

checkpoints.title: Refuse bad numbers
checkpoints.description: The ScoutEntry constructor throws an IllegalArgumentException, with a message, for a team or match of 0 or less, or negative points.

checkpoints.title: Your own exception
checkpoints.description: BadLineException is a checked exception (it extends Exception) that keeps its message and the line number it was made with.

checkpoints.title: Read one line
checkpoints.description: ScoutParser.parseLine turns "team,match,points" into a ScoutEntry, and throws a BadLineException for anything it can't read.

checkpoints.title: Skip and count
checkpoints.description: ScoutParser.parseAll reads every line, catching BadLineException to record a bad line's number and keep going. Blank lines are skipped.

checkpoints.title: Always stop
checkpoints.description: SafeAuto.runStep returns true when a step finishes and false when it throws, and stops the drivetrain in a finally block either way.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.description: Write code once and use it for any type: a Pair that holds a team and its nickname, a RingBuffer that keeps the last few sensor readings, and methods that work on a list of anything, or anything that can be compared.

checkpoints.title: A generic Pair
checkpoints.description: Pair<A, B> holds two values of any two types: Pair(A first, B second), getFirst() and getSecond().

checkpoints.title: A RingBuffer of anything
checkpoints.description: RingBuffer<T> keeps only the newest capacity items: add drops the oldest when it's full; size, get (0 = oldest) and latest (null when empty).

checkpoints.title: A generic method
checkpoints.description: ListTools.lastOrDefault is <T> T lastOrDefault(List<T> items, T fallback): the last item, or fallback for an empty list.

checkpoints.title: A bounded type
checkpoints.description: ListTools.max is <T extends Comparable<T>> T max(List<T> items): the biggest item by compareTo, the first one on a tie, or null for an empty list.

lessons.title: Big-O & Efficiency
lessons.description: Count the steps your code takes. Sort snippets into O(1), O(log n), O(n) and O(n²), then speed up a scouting app's duplicate-team check from millions of steps to a few thousand with a HashSet.

checkpoints.title: Classify the snippets
checkpoints.description: Every snippet in Answers.java is marked CONSTANT, LOG_N, LINEAR or N_SQUARED correctly.

checkpoints.title: One step, one pass
checkpoints.description: ScoutStats.latest returns the last score in one look (O(1)) and ScoutStats.best returns the highest in one pass (O(n)); both return 0 for an empty list.

checkpoints.title: A fast duplicate check
checkpoints.description: Duplicates.hasDuplicate gives the same answer as hasDuplicateSlow, but looks at each team only once by using a HashSet (O(n) instead of O(n²)).

checkpoints.title: Teams at both events
checkpoints.description: EventOverlap.teamsInBoth counts the different teams that appear in both lists, in O(n + m) steps.

lessons.title: Searching & Sorting
lessons.description: Find a team in a long list, first one item at a time and then by halving with binary search. Sort scouted teams by score with a sort you write yourself, then rank them the way real code does, with List.sort and a Comparator.

checkpoints.title: Linear search
checkpoints.description: Search.indexOf returns the index of the first matching team, or -1, and stops looking as soon as it finds one.

checkpoints.title: Binary search
checkpoints.description: Search.binarySearch finds a team in a sorted list, or returns -1, in about log2(n) looks, with a loop you write yourself.

checkpoints.title: Sort it yourself
checkpoints.description: Sorting.sortByScore puts an array of teams in order, highest score first, with a selection or insertion sort written by hand.

checkpoints.title: Rankings with a Comparator
checkpoints.description: Sorting.rankings returns a new list ranked by score, highest first, with ties going to the lower team number, and leaves the list it was given alone.

lessons.title: Stacks & Queues
lessons.description: Give the dashboard an Undo button, catch bracket typos in a typed-in auto, run auto steps in order, and build the indexer's line of game pieces by hand. Learn when the newest thing comes out first and when the oldest does.

checkpoints.title: Undo with a stack
checkpoints.description: SettingHistory keeps old values in an ArrayDeque used as a stack: set saves the old value, undo goes back to the newest saved one (and does nothing when there is none), undoCount counts them.

checkpoints.title: Balanced brackets
checkpoints.description: AutoParser.isBalanced uses a stack to check that every ( [ { in an auto string is closed by its own kind of bracket, in the right order.

checkpoints.title: Auto steps in a queue
checkpoints.description: AutoQueue keeps steps in an ArrayDeque used as a queue: nextStep returns the oldest step first, and "done" when none are left.

checkpoints.title: A queue by hand
checkpoints.description: IndexerQueue is a fixed-size queue built on a plain array: load refuses when full, fire returns the oldest piece (or "empty"), and the slots wrap round to the start.

lessons.title: Trees
lessons.description: Keep every team at the event in a binary search tree that stays sorted as you add to it, then count the actions in an auto shaped like the robot's behavior trees. Recursion does the walking.

checkpoints.title: Insert and find
checkpoints.description: TeamTree.insert puts lower team numbers to the left and higher ones to the right (no repeats); contains and size work on any tree.

checkpoints.title: In order
checkpoints.description: TeamTree.inOrder returns every team, lowest number first, by visiting left, node, right.

checkpoints.title: Height
checkpoints.description: TeamTree.height counts the nodes on the longest path from the root down: 0 for an empty tree, 1 for one team.

checkpoints.title: An auto tree
checkpoints.description: AutoNode.countActions counts the nodes with no children, and AutoNode.depth measures the longest path down, in a tree where a node can have any number of children.

lessons.title: Graphs
lessons.description: Map the field as waypoints joined by lanes, then search it: find out whether the robot can get somewhere at all, the path with the fewest hops, and which waypoints a blocked lane cuts off.

checkpoints.title: The field map
checkpoints.description: FieldMap keeps a Map<String, List<String>> of waypoints. connect(a, b) joins two waypoints both ways, once, and neighbors() never returns null.

checkpoints.title: Can the robot get there?
checkpoints.description: PathFinder.canReach searches the map, remembering where it has been, and says whether one waypoint can be reached from another.

checkpoints.title: Fewest hops
checkpoints.description: PathFinder.shortestPath uses a breadth-first search to return a path with the fewest hops, or an empty list when there isn't one.

checkpoints.title: Cut off
checkpoints.description: PathFinder.unreachable lists, in alphabetical order, every waypoint the robot can't get to from where it starts.

lessons.title: Design Patterns
lessons.description: Use three named shapes for classes on a pretend robot: swap drive modes with Strategy, tell the LEDs and intake about a game piece with Observer, and build the right auto from its name with Factory.

checkpoints.title: Two drive modes
checkpoints.description: TankDrive and ArcadeDrive implement DriveMode; arcade mixes forward and turn and clamps each side between -1 and 1.

checkpoints.title: Swap the strategy
checkpoints.description: Drivetrain holds a DriveMode, drives with whichever one it has, and switches with setMode (ignoring null).

checkpoints.title: Tell the listeners
checkpoints.description: BeamBreak adds and removes listeners, and update() tells each of them, in order, only when the reading changes.

checkpoints.title: The auto factory
checkpoints.description: AutoFactory.create builds a new auto from a dashboard name, ignoring case and spaces, with Do nothing for anything it doesn't know.
